caption: What if you walked inside a cloud? If you live in North India, you already have. Winter fog is basically a cloud sitting on the ground, and dense fog rolled over Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh this month. The IMD calls fog 'very dense' when you can't see even 50 metres, which is why trains crawl. Each cloud droplet is only about 0.02 mm wide, and it takes about a million of them to make one raindrop. They fall only about 1 cm a second, so gentle rising air keeps them floating. Still, a puffy cloud 1 km on each side holds about 500 tonnes of water, roughly 100 elephants. But it's spread thin: a bedroom full of cloud holds only about 25 grams. Plot twist: on a cold morning, the breath you puff out is a tiny cloud too. Driving in fog? Go slow and use fog lights. Would YOU walk into a cloud? 👇
